title: First research pass: generic brief-to-voice-agent builder

scope.purpose: Ground a generic competition builder in primary literature and the official kit, with ranked practical recommendations.
scope.source_composition: Nine research papers and one official documentation family.
scope.constraints: Analysis only. No source-code changes, synthetic-case generation, exporter-compatibility implementation, live Freya calls, or credentials inspection/output.
scope.status: First research pass complete; recommendations have not been implemented or measured in this workspace.

evidence_labels.supported_finding: A directly inspected official-kit requirement or an author-reported method/result. It is not independent replication or proof of effectiveness here.
evidence_labels.inference: A reasoned architectural transfer or proposed acceptance criterion; no competition-specific measured gain is claimed.
evidence_labels.unverified_idea: An additional hypothesis requiring bounded local validation before adoption.
evidence_labels.access_limitation: A documented source-access constraint; unavailable evidence is not invented.

methods.requested_paper: Closely read the requested τ-bench PDF main body, evaluation details and consequential appendix examples; cross-checked with arXiv v1 full HTML. Abstract-only reading was not used.
methods.page_convention: All PDF locators are one-based physical pages of the explicitly linked version, not printed journal pagination. For institutional manuscripts, covers and appendices can change numbering. HTML section locators are used when PDF pages are unavailable.
methods.pdf_visual_access: PDF text and full HTML were available. Requested page screenshots were rejected because the web screenshot facility was disabled; no visual render verification is claimed. The reports are plain text/JSON, so no PDF artifact was authored.
methods.selection: Sources were chosen for policy-constrained execution, constrained workflow generation, bounded agent design, user-simulator fidelity, assertion-based state checking, oracle independence, mutation/metamorphic testing and stateful voice orchestration.
review_limits: This is a focused first pass, not a systematic review or exhaustive search.
Reported benchmark results are attributed to their authors and are not independently reproduced.
SimulatorArena PDF fetches exceeded the browser size limit; verified HTML sections are cited without fabricated page numbers.
LiveKit is rolling, undated documentation; its access date is reported rather than assigning a publication year.
No reviewed source proves complete automatic compilation of unseen, amended collections briefs.
No live agent, simulator, policy mutation or runtime/exporter experiment was run in this literature task.

executive_assessment.label: inference
executive_assessment.conclusion: The best-supported design direction is constrained compilation: a provenance-linked policy representation and normalized tool contract, deterministic guards for consequential actions, a shared ordered product ledger, and separately derived state and temporal checks. A few conversation phases can realize the flow while preserving state. Automatic extraction completeness and runtime interruption behavior remain the main unresolved engineering questions.
executive_assessment.practical_first_slice: Before expanding search or persona complexity, make source coverage, identity/confirmation gates, calendar calculations, per-product commitment state and transfer/closing precedence inspectable in a local mock. Coordinate implementation and cases with their existing owners.

recommended_architecture.label: inference

steps.name: Input normalization
steps.output: Brief/amendment source spans and an API contract with fields, enums, return values and side effects.

steps.name: Policy compilation
steps.output: Typed rules with call/product scope, precedence, parameters, required speech, forbidden actions and unresolved conflicts.

steps.name: Guarded call state
steps.output: Deterministic calendar and amount logic, identity and retry state, ordered product ledger, confirmation snapshots and allowed tool actions.

steps.name: Conversation realization
steps.output: Scoped phase instructions; typed interpretation of fragments/corrections; question answering and resumption; shared authoritative state.

steps.name: Independent verification
steps.output: Source-derived expected records, temporal event checks, speech obligations, policy mutations, validated metamorphic relations and simulator-fidelity annotations.

steps.name: Bounded repair and delivery
steps.output: Diagnosed fixes within the elapsed-time budget, retained last valid candidate and full build trace.

recommended_architecture.scope_boundary: This describes interfaces and responsibilities for the builder owners. It does not specify or verify Freya export syntax, generate a test corpus or propose an alternative runtime.

competition_grounding.label: supported_finding
competition_grounding.finding: The final run must automatically read unseen material, derive changed rule values and tool fields, and finish within 30 minutes including tests. Final-brief content cannot be manually inserted into builder code or prompts. A build trace is required.

competition_grounding.label: supported_finding
competition_grounding.finding: Scoring requires exact bank records, policy adherence and honesty, with no partial credit. Hidden customers run three times and count only if all three pass; calendar days vary.

competition_grounding.label: supported_finding
competition_grounding.finding: Identity, disclosure, refusal and retry rules are stateful. Calendar calculations use the injected now; holidays, amount floors, bands and deadlines come from the brief.

competition_grounding.label: supported_finding
competition_grounding.finding: A promise requires a read-back and clear confirmation, can be corrected before recording, cannot be changed after recording, and can be described as recorded only after ok:true. Failed recording is retried once.

competition_grounding.label: supported_finding
competition_grounding.finding: Brief B overrides A selectively: attempts/deadlines are per product, account order matters, all proposed promises share a read-back and confirmation, and each product is recorded separately. Partial recording success is retained.

competition_grounding.label: supported_finding
competition_grounding.finding: Any Brief B transfer prohibits all add_note calls before or after transfer. Restructuring retains recorded promises but discards agreements not recorded. Without transfer, unresolved products require notes; closing follows the stated reduction over account order.

competition_grounding.label: supported_finding
competition_grounding.finding: close_call occurs exactly once as the last tool call after goodbye. In Brief A, transfer overrides a recorded promise. Hardship takes priority over persuasion and restructuring rules.

competition_grounding.label: supported_finding
competition_grounding.finding: Customers fragment numbers, correct values, ask questions back, use verbal amounts/dates and digress. Tests serialize per workspace; long silent turns can cause hangs or customer abandonment.

sources.title: τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
sources.read_scope: Main text §§1-6, PDF pp.1-9; Appendix A p.13; B.1 API and policy examples pp.13-19; selected B.2/C.1 construction examples pp.20-24; C.2.1-C.2.3 annotations and consequential trajectory steps pp.25-42. Long inventory dumps were inspected selectively, not reproduced.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: Deterministic database tools and hidden user goals form a partially observed environment. Reward checks database equality and required response substrings; it can miss confirmation violations.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: Pass^k requires all k trials to succeed. Its estimator averages C(c_i,k)/C(n_i,k) over tasks.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: GPT-4o function calling scores 61.2% retail, 35.2% airline, 48.2% domain-weighted average; retail pass^8 falls below 25%.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: Of 40 audited failures, four involved annotation issues; among 36 agent failures, argument/information errors comprise about 55%, decisions 25%, compound requests 19%.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: Native function calling beats text-formatted baselines; adding a think function did not improve their tested agents.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: Task curation targets unique outcomes and uses human refinement. Simulator reasoning, memory, instruction fidelity and curation bias remain limitations.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: Examples show a premature single-item exchange and omitted updates to other orders.

limitations.label: supported_finding
limitations.text: Table 3 prints an airline baseline of 33.2%, whereas Table 2 prints 35.2%; do not silently reconcile them.

limitations.label: inference
limitations.text: These 2024 text-agent baselines do not establish today's fixed Freya model performance, voice latency, or the efficacy of our proposed compiler.

builder_implication.label: inference
builder_implication.text: Use bank-state assertions plus temporal conversation checks; optimize repeated consistency and complete per-product obligations. Move numerical and calendar policy execution into generated code where the platform permits it.

sources.title: FlowAgent: Achieving Compliance and Flexibility for Workflow Agents
sources.read_scope: §§3-6 methods, evaluation, result tables and controller ablation; §8 limitations; appendix PDL example and workflow representation.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: PDL combines API/ANSWER node prerequisites with natural language and pseudocode. Pre-decision guidance and post-decision checks constrain dependencies and repeated actions.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: GPT-4o in-house success is 67.72% versus 62.50% for ReAct-NL; OOW success is 32.01% versus 18.03%. On ordinary SGD, FlowAgent's 32.79% is below ReAct-NL's 34.62%.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: Removing controllers reduces success in the reported OOW ablation.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: Evaluation uses LLM-simulated users and an LLM judge. Workflows are manually constructed; automated workflow generation is explicitly outside the study.

limitations.label: inference
limitations.text: The prose claim of universal superiority is stronger than Table 3 supports. This is an execution design reference, not evidence that arbitrary briefs can be compiled correctly.

limitations.label: inference
limitations.text: A procedural graph alone does not model Freya's calendar arithmetic, future transfer constraints, or irreversible partial commits.

builder_implication.label: inference
builder_implication.text: Represent policy as explicit predicates and guarded actions, while allowing bounded question answering and corrections between steps. Generate the guards from the brief instead of copying a fixed PDL workflow.

sources.title: Automated Design of Agentic Systems
sources.version: arXiv:2408.08435v1 (15 August 2024); later ICLR 2025 publication exists
sources.read_scope: §§2-4, code-space search, refinement and evaluation protocol, held-out results and transfer table.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: Meta Agent Search generates agent code, refines proposals, evaluates validation data, and archives designs with metrics and bootstrap confidence intervals.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: Table 1 reports DROP F1 79.4 versus best listed manual baseline 65.8; MGSM accuracy 53.4% versus 39.0%. These are held-out results after 30 search iterations.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: ARC uses 20 validation and 60 test questions, repeated five times, and 25 search iterations.

limitations.label: inference
limitations.text: Static reasoning benchmarks and permissive code search do not validate live banking policy adherence. Their search budget does not fit a 30-minute Freya build with serialized simulations.

limitations.label: inference
limitations.text: Repeated validation-driven selection can overfit the practice suite; the paper's held-out evaluation matters more than discovery-archive rankings.

builder_implication.label: inference
builder_implication.text: Adopt a bounded build-check-repair loop with structured feedback and a retained best valid candidate. Search within a validated policy schema and permitted workflow primitives, not arbitrary live agent designs.

sources.title: τ²-Bench: Evaluating Conversational Agents in a Dual-Control Environment
sources.read_scope: §§3-4 task construction, assertion-based evaluation, ablations, simulator audit; Appendix A.1 personas.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: Atomic tasks separate initialization, solution and final-state assertions; compositions are checked by executing solutions and verifying assertions.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: No-user versus dual-control ablations distinguish reasoning from communication/coordination difficulties.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: Two annotators audit trajectories. Telecom has 8/50 simulator-error conversations, including 3/50 critical errors; retail has 20/50, including 6/50 critical errors.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: Table 2's caption says no critical telecom errors, but its row and nearby prose report three (6%).

limitations.label: inference
limitations.text: Cross-domain error rates are not a controlled causal estimate of tool-constrained simulation. Customer agency in telecom differs from a collections call.

limitations.label: inference
limitations.text: Task assertions establish correctness relative to their encoded model, not independently against an original banking brief.

builder_implication.label: inference
builder_implication.text: Keep persona facts separate from speech style and audit scenario fidelity. Diagnose deterministic policy logic with tool mocks separately from conversational realization; do not let the agent's own claimed success decide the oracle.

sources.title: SimulatorArena: Are User Simulators Reliable Proxies for Multi-Turn Evaluation of AI Assistants?
sources.read_scope: Full relevant HTML §§2-5, simulator profile construction, human study, rating alignment and behavioral-attribute failures.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: The benchmark contains 909 conversations from 107 participants on math tutoring and document creation.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: Profiles improve reported human-rating Spearman correlation from 0.61 to 0.77 in tutoring and 0.55 to 0.70 in document creation.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: Richer profiles can reduce fulfillment of interaction-style attributes; optimal profiles differ between tasks.

limitations.label: supported_finding
limitations.text: Messages are also assessed by an LLM judge; the study covers two text tasks.

limitations.label: inference
limitations.text: These correlations are not per-call agreement rates or evidence of banking-policy coverage. Do not import real participant data into this synthetic-data competition.

limitations.label: access_limitation
limitations.text: Publisher and arXiv PDFs exceeded the browser fetch size limit. Exact HTML sections are verified; PDF page numbers are deliberately omitted.

builder_implication.label: inference
builder_implication.text: Use a small number of enforceable behavioral attributes. Check whether a simulated customer actually corrects, fragments or asks back as requested; persona labels alone do not establish test coverage.

sources.title: How Effectively Does Metamorphic Testing Alleviate the Oracle Problem?
sources.version: Author manuscript in institutional repository; one repository cover page precedes manuscript page 1
sources.read_scope: Study design and expert relation validation; §VI-B results and Figure 2; threat and generalization discussion.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: Trainers and co-authors validate proposed relations before testing, discarding invalid relations.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: Across five algorithmic programs, three to six relations on average recover at least 90% of the fault-detection improvement from random testing to random testing with an oracle.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: Some individual testers' relation sets remain statistically less effective than the complete oracle.

limitations.label: inference
limitations.text: The 90% measure is a fraction of an improvement gap, not 90% of all faults. Controlled algorithm/mutant studies do not establish the same effect for stochastic conversations.

limitations.label: inference
limitations.text: A metamorphic relation is only valid where the policy makes its proposed invariance necessary; common wrong behavior can satisfy a relation.

builder_implication.label: inference
builder_implication.text: Use policy-preserving transformations to expose parser and runtime defects, but retain direct expected-state and temporal checks. Validate each relation against source requirements before using it.

sources.title: Are Mutants a Valid Substitute for Real Faults in Software Testing?
sources.read_scope: §2 methodology; §3 results, mutation coupling, coverage controls and threats.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: The study uses 357 real faults in five applications totaling 321,000 lines, developer/generated suites and approximately 230,000 mutants.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: Mutant detection correlates with real-fault detection beyond statement coverage. Reported coupling covers 73% of faults; 10% need stronger/new operators and 17% are not coupled.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: Fault selection and available mutation operators limit generalization.

limitations.label: inference
limitations.text: Mutation score is a fault-detection proxy, not a correctness certificate. Java syntactic mutations do not represent all omitted policy clauses or voice misunderstandings.

builder_implication.label: inference
builder_implication.text: Evaluate the local oracle with targeted policy mutants: bypass confirmation, include holidays, change retry limits, omit a product note, remove transfer precedence, or confuse proposed with recorded promises. Report survivors by obligation, including unreachable/equivalent mutants.

sources.title: Workflows; Agents and handoffs (LiveKit Agents documentation)
sources.year_note: Undated rolling official documentation, accessed 10 October 2026
sources.read_scope: Core constructs, Choosing a pattern, Best practices; agent handoff and Passing state sections.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: Documentation distinguishes persistent session control, typed short-lived tasks, ordered task groups and full agent handoffs.
evidence.section: Workflows: Core constructs and Choosing a pattern

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: It recommends starting with one agent; added patterns introduce latency or context-management overhead, and splits should address concrete limitations.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: Session userdata stores typed shared state; handoffs require explicit handling of conversation context.
evidence.section: Agents and handoffs: Passing state and Context preservation

limitations.label: inference
limitations.text: These are product capabilities and guidance, not controlled score or latency measurements. LiveKit abstractions are not Freya exporter capabilities; no LiveKit runtime migration is recommended here.

builder_implication.label: inference
builder_implication.text: Compile a small number of conversation phases with one authoritative typed call state. Preserve partial identity answers, confirmation snapshots, retry counters and committed records across phase changes; minimize unnecessary conversational handoffs.

sources.title: An Experimental Evaluation of the Assumption of Independence in Multi-Version Programming
sources.version: Institutional-hosted manuscript/technical-report layout with appendix; PDF locators below refer to that 47-page file
sources.read_scope: §§1-5 experimental independence and results; §6 examples of correlated faults; §7 external-validity discussion.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: Twenty-seven independently developed versions from two universities undergo one million tests; 1,255 inputs make multiple versions fail. The independence model is rejected.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: Shared numerical and geometric misunderstandings cause correlated faults despite separate implementations.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: The programs are small and authors discuss student-participant and industrial-generalization limitations.

limitations.label: inference
limitations.text: This is evidence about human-written software, not measured LLM error correlations. It supports caution about assumed independence; it does not quantify benefits of using different models.

builder_implication.label: inference
builder_implication.text: Have the checker derive obligations directly from source spans and use a separately implemented reference calculator. Different prompts/models are useful diversity but not proof of oracle independence; a shared mistaken policy extraction can invalidate both.

sources.title: FlowMind: Automatic Workflow Generation with LLMs
sources.year_note: ICAIF 2023 publication; arXiv v1 deposited in 2024
sources.read_scope: §3 two-stage workflow generation; §4 dataset, API grounding, ablations, result table and feedback example.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: A context/API/code lecture precedes generated workflow code. API declarations describe arguments and outputs; execution uses the provided functions.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: On 600 financial QA questions, no-feedback accuracy is 99.5%, 99.0%, 89.5% for easy/intermediate/hard versus 63.5%, 28.0%, 8.5% for context retrieval.

evidence.label: supported_finding
evidence.claim: The retrieval baseline truncates context; human feedback further improves accuracy, and semantically poor API descriptions harm generation.

limitations.label: inference
limitations.text: This compiles information-query workflows, not dense amended SOPs or ongoing voice policies. Its large gain partly reflects the constrained API setup and weak truncated baseline.

limitations.label: inference
limitations.text: The human-feedback branch cannot be part of the competition's final no-manual-step run. Proprietary-data isolation is an architectural claim, not a security proof.

builder_implication.label: inference
builder_implication.text: Give the builder a normalized tool catalog derived from each supplied API, including fields, enums, success indicators and side effects. Generate against a constrained contract and verify bindings before emitting a workflow.

ranked_recommendations.label: inference
ranked_recommendations.title: Compile briefs into an evidence-linked policy representation before generating the agent.
ranked_recommendations.action: Extract atomic rules, definitions, tables, exceptions, precedence and amendments into a typed intermediate representation. Each record should carry original source spans, scope (call/product), conditions, obligations, numeric/calendar parameters and matching tool-schema fields. Resolve B-over-A and memo-over-policy precedence explicitly. Preserve unresolved conflicts rather than silently inventing a rule.
ranked_recommendations.why_for_competition: This gives the generic builder a place to detect skipped rules and separates reusable compiler behavior from brief-specific values.
ranked_recommendations.acceptance: Every normative source clause is covered by an IR record or explicitly accounted for; every parameter and tool enum traces to the input; amendment resolution has a provenance trail. Different values, identity questions and outcome labels require no source-code change.
ranked_recommendations.uncertainty: No reviewed paper demonstrates complete automatic extraction of this competition's unseen, amended bank briefs. This is the central engineering hypothesis, not a solved literature result.

ranked_recommendations.label: inference
ranked_recommendations.title: Use a deterministic policy kernel for consequential decisions.
ranked_recommendations.action: Generate calendar arithmetic, amount checks, retry counters, identity gates, per-product attempts, permissible tool arguments and closing reduction as code or guards. Let the language model extract typed user events and render required speech; let code determine legal transitions and writes. Gate debt information until identity completes and success claims until the backend result permits them.
ranked_recommendations.why_for_competition: A correct-looking dialogue still fails if one date, product, reason or tool ordering is wrong.
ranked_recommendations.acceptance: For a supplied typed event, the next legal action set and policy state are reproducible. Boundary calculations use the call's now and extracted calendar; invalid actions are rejected before execution.
ranked_recommendations.uncertainty: Natural-language interpretation remains fallible. Code guards do not prove the parser, transcription or rule extraction correct.

ranked_recommendations.label: inference
ranked_recommendations.title: Track proposed, confirmed and recorded promises separately and defer note writes.
ranked_recommendations.action: Maintain an ordered product ledger with proposed amount/date, confirmation revision, recorded result, failure count and unresolved reason. A correction invalidates the relevant confirmation snapshot. Commit only confirmed values, retain successful product writes on later failures, and never retry a successful write. Keep prospective notes in local state until a non-transfer closing path is fixed; then write notes and close. Transfer paths discard pending notes and unrecorded agreements.
ranked_recommendations.why_for_competition: Brief B forbids notes even before a later transfer and distinguishes recorded promises from verbal agreements; eager note writes create an irreversible policy breach.
ranked_recommendations.acceptance: A mock run with one successful product, one failed product and a subsequent transfer keeps the successful promise, creates no notes and selects transfer closure. No product is omitted and no successful promise is duplicated.
ranked_recommendations.uncertainty: The finalization boundary and interruption behavior must be checked by the runtime/exporter owner. Deferral is a proposed solution, not a verified Freya behavior. A transfer arriving while final writes execute remains a runtime race to audit.

ranked_recommendations.label: inference
ranked_recommendations.title: Build the oracle from the source requirements through a separate implementation path.
ranked_recommendations.action: Have a checker independently read source spans and compile expected records and invariants; do not import the runtime's result-producing helpers as the expected-answer calculator. Combine final-state checks with tool-event ordering and transcript obligations. Give any language-model judge explicit rule IDs and evidence spans, then retain its rationale and uncertainty.
ranked_recommendations.why_for_competition: The runtime and checker can agree on the same wrongly extracted holiday, threshold or precedence. State equality alone also misses disclosure, confirmation and honest failure reporting.
ranked_recommendations.acceptance: An intentionally wrong calendar or confirmation gate is rejected by the checker even if runtime state looks internally consistent. Final-state, temporal-policy and speech checks report separately.
ranked_recommendations.uncertainty: Different models or prompts do not establish statistical independence. Source-based independent checking reduces one form of common error but cannot eliminate all shared interpretations.

ranked_recommendations.label: inference
ranked_recommendations.title: Measure whether the oracle detects realistic policy mutations.
ranked_recommendations.action: Seed targeted local mutants that bypass confirmation, mishandle holidays, alter retry/attempt bounds, suppress an unresolved-product note, lose product order, remove transfer precedence or assert recorded success after a failed tool. Evaluate whether existing tests reject them. Separate uncovered, unreachable and behaviorally equivalent mutants.
ranked_recommendations.why_for_competition: Rule and line coverage can look complete while a checker never notices missing obligations.
ranked_recommendations.acceptance: The local test owner reports killed and surviving mutants by source obligation, and a passing baseline fails when each selected critical fault is injected.
ranked_recommendations.uncertainty: Mutation scores do not predict a hidden customer pass rate; policy omission and speech-understanding faults need dedicated operators.

ranked_recommendations.label: inference
ranked_recommendations.title: Use metamorphic checks with explicit preconditions.
ranked_recommendations.action: Test opaque-ID renaming with consistent backend remapping; table/prose rewrites and reordered independent paragraphs; equivalent amount/date wording; and irrelevant digressions that do not change policy-relevant facts. Compare canonical bank results and obligations, not verbatim transcripts. Treat corrections and reordered products as controlled changes where the expected answer may change.
ranked_recommendations.why_for_competition: Final material can change form, and final customers preserve facts while changing delivery. These transformations test generic parsing and state continuity.
ranked_recommendations.acceptance: Each relation states why semantics are preserved and which output is compared. A paragraph-order relation excludes chronology-dependent amendments. A date-shift relation, if added, shifts all temporal data and preserves weekday/calendar structure.
ranked_recommendations.uncertainty: Brief B product permutation is not an invariance: first unresolved non-paid product and negotiation order can change. Extra refusals or post-confirmation corrections are not harmless paraphrases.

ranked_recommendations.label: inference
ranked_recommendations.title: Evaluate repeated consistency and simulator fidelity together.
ranked_recommendations.action: Keep semantic scenario facts fixed across style variants and reruns. Require customer facts and behavioral attributes to remain faithful to the intended scenario; flag simulator errors separately. Track per-case triples, rule failures, product count and style, alongside single-run success. Reserve independent held-out practice variations for candidate selection.
ranked_recommendations.why_for_competition: The final counts all-three-pass customers. One green run cannot justify reliability, and simulator drift can distort diagnosis.
ranked_recommendations.acceptance: A customer passes a local triple only after three valid passing trajectories. Simulator failures remain visible rather than being silently discarded; official scorer results remain authoritative.
ranked_recommendations.uncertainty: Synthetic personas are stress tests, not proof of human realism. Three successes are a selection observation, not a precise estimate of true reliability. Repeats across dates/styles need stratified reporting, not an unjustified IID assumption.

ranked_recommendations.label: inference
ranked_recommendations.title: Give each conversation phase scoped instructions and shared authoritative state.
ranked_recommendations.action: Start with a few phases such as opening, identity, account/negotiation, confirmation/recording and closure, plus a common event dispatcher for questions and transfers. Carry all counters and product state across phase transitions. Accumulate partial numeric answers and apply corrections before emitting completed typed values; resume the pending question after permitted answers back.
ranked_recommendations.why_for_competition: Briefs require one-at-a-time identity questions and natural customer interruptions, while long silent turns can lose calls.
ranked_recommendations.acceptance: Phase changes preserve identity status, remaining attempts, candidate values and committed records. A question back does not reset progress, consume an attempt incorrectly or trigger a premature write.
ranked_recommendations.uncertainty: There is no measured basis here for a specific optimal node count. Physical turn detection and Freya route semantics belong to the runtime owner's validation.

ranked_recommendations.label: inference
ranked_recommendations.title: Bound build-check-repair search by the competition clock.
ranked_recommendations.action: Do source/IR/schema checks and local deterministic checks before an authorized live practice run. Repair the highest-impact diagnosed defect, rerun only when a new change justifies it, and retain the last valid candidate. Record each model call's purpose and timing. Reserve time to finalize the result and trace; use local tests to avoid spending the budget on repeated full simulations.
ranked_recommendations.why_for_competition: One simulation runs at a time, practice runs can take 3-11 minutes, and all work must fit the 30-minute cap.
ranked_recommendations.acceptance: The builder uses elapsed-time checks and a bounded retry count, always produces a trace, and does not schedule a test that would consume its finalization reserve.
ranked_recommendations.uncertainty: ADAS's 25-30 search iterations and FlowMind's human-feedback improvements do not transfer directly. Optimal time allocation must be measured locally.

ranked_recommendations.label: unverified_idea
ranked_recommendations.title: Use a second extraction view to find omitted or conflicting rules.
ranked_recommendations.action: Compare a source-order rule extraction with a separate extraction organized around tool preconditions, outcomes and forbidden actions. Ask the checker to identify disagreements by source span rather than vote on a preferred answer. Maintain a capability registry for requirements that cannot yet be represented.
ranked_recommendations.why_for_competition: Raw bank emails, memos and code lists may express exceptions indirectly or amend earlier rules.
ranked_recommendations.acceptance: A deliberately omitted exception or contradictory amendment is surfaced with both source spans before workflow generation.
ranked_recommendations.uncertainty: This has no competition-specific measured result. Run it only if bounded cost and extraction-recall improvements justify the extra model call.

cautions.label: inference
cautions.text: Policy extraction, runtime and oracle must not share one unexamined interpretation of a brief. Distinct model names or prompts are not evidence of statistical independence.

cautions.label: inference
cautions.text: Database equality is necessary but not sufficient where permission, disclosure, ordering and truthful speech are scored. Keep these failure classes inspectable.

cautions.label: inference
cautions.text: Repeated success should be recorded per scenario. Cubing an aggregate single-run pass rate is not a justified estimate of the official all-three score: scenario heterogeneity and correlated trials matter.

cautions.label: inference
cautions.text: A policy-preserving transformation requires explicit preconditions. Product order, a new refusal, chronology-dependent amendments or a post-confirmation correction can change the correct outcome.

cautions.label: inference
cautions.text: Persona labels and more nodes do not establish coverage or realism. Prefer observable scenario fidelity and specific state-preservation checks.

cautions.label: unverified_idea
cautions.text: A second rule-extraction view may reveal omissions, but its benefit and cost need measurement before it consumes the final-run budget.
